items.title: Jason Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: the bassist at the time, Roland Guerin, had a conductor’s score

ctx.x: We did a lot of things. There was a lot of different projects he was doing. I think that’s why some may say that I left Hombres to play with Marcus. I was already playing with Marcus, but I was in school, and there was a lot going on, even in his group. We did this record, Blues for the New Millennium, where it was me and Ali Jackson were playing two drums for some of the record. Not all of it. But some tunes he’d play. Some tunes I’d play. Then some tunes we’d play together. Ali was in place of me, because I was…

piano show. But we were lucky. We had three days where all we could do was practice. I remember preparing for this piece. It was great, because I had a score of Gershwin’s transcript, and the bassist at the time, Roland Guerin, had a conductor’s score, and Marcus had a Braille score. We all had scores. I loved working on that, because we all said, all right, how are we going to do this? What can we do? Because we wanted to deal with taking that into the jazz idiom, but still playing with classical musicians. So…
So you’re saying it’s just the rhythm section. You three are coming up with the arrangement, the conception for this.
